title: who-gets-the-raise: replication package for 'Who Gets the Raise? Japan's Public Works Pay Rates and the Wages of Security Guards'
description:
Replication package for Kazi Affnann Azom (2026), "Who Gets the Raise? Japan's Public Works Pay Rates and the Wages of Security Guards." Every year Japan's Ministry of Land, Infrastructure, Transport and Tourism sets the public works design labor rates, the daily wage that cost estimates for public works assume for each trade in each prefecture, including traffic guards employed by security companies. The package compares the official rate for traffic guards with security guards' pay in the Basic Survey on Wage Structure and with prefecture minimum wages, for the 47 prefectures from 2012 to 2025, and adds the occupation that includes traffic guards, other protective service workers, for 2020 to 2025.

It contains the dated analysis plan, written before any test was run and committed as the first file of the repository, with its change log; the data files, copied unchanged from japan-guard-price-panel v1.2.1 (doi:10.5281/zenodo.23856290); the code that builds the prefecture-year panel, runs the planned tests and checks and the analyses added after the main results were seen; tests of the estimator on simulated data; and the results, tables and figures.

Code: MIT (see LICENSE). The author's text, plan, results, tables and figures: CC BY 4.0 (see LICENSE-DATA). The data are compiled from 公共工事設計労務単価 (MLIT) and 地域別最低賃金改定状況 (MHLW), used under the Public Data License 1.0, and from 賃金構造基本統計調査 (MHLW, via e-Stat), used under e-Stat's terms of use; they are edited from the official files and are not official products of either ministry.
